title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-12-07
source: Source: sbd > Bear's cassette master  (probably) > dat (Rob Eaton) > dat (44k) - Provided by Tim Dalton; Transfer: Dat > Sony PCM-R500 > Tascam DA-3000 > wav 16/44.1 - Transferred by Charlie Miller; Lineage: wav 16/44.1 > iZotope RX6 Advanced > iZotope Ozone 5 Advanced > CD Wave >Flac16; edited and mastered SIRMick

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with a bit of hiss captures a fiery late‑1969 single‑set show featuring a dark‑star‑ish Dancin' and a primal The Eleven → Love Light sequence.
ai_review.review: The set delivers high‑energy Pigpen numbers, a surprising Black Peter opener, and a standout jam on Dancin' that veers into Dark Star territory before exploding into The Eleven > Love Light. The soundboard source is generally clear but has some hiss at the very beginning, which doesn’t detract much from the overall enjoyment.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong musical performance with several highlighted jams outweighs minor recording hiss; three reviews provide enough detail for a confident but not definitive rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Noticeable hiss on the opening Black Peter track and slight uncertainty about completeness of the set, but overall clear mix with well‑balanced instruments.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A single‑set, eclectic mix that foreshadows the acoustic/electric blend of 1970; heavy Altamont vibe but the crowd stays engaged throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Dark‑Star‑like improvisation on Dancin' and a powerful first solo jam leading into The Eleven.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal on Mama Tried is highlighted; his rhythm work supports the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ adds melodic texture, especially noted during The Eleven > Love Light.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann drives the Good Lovin' → Drums → Good Lovin' transition and underpins the high‑energy jams.
